# Evaluation report (auto-generated by `roomfinder evaluate`)

## 1. Data quality the pipeline handles
- 3,426 overlapping class pairs (3,630 timetable rows involved); 24 event-event and 1,337 class-event overlaps.
- 40% of classes exceed their room's capacity.
- 49% of events start outside 08:00-20:00; they still block their room.
- Expected vs actual event attendance correlation: -0.00 (not used as ground truth).

## 2. Allocation policies (simulated replay, cancelled requests excluded)
- Upper bound: 98.0% of requests have at least one feasible room given existing occupancy.

| policy | order | placed | placement rate | unmet placed | mean wasted seats |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| first_fit | chronological | 4,144 | 96.8% | 1,513/1,559 | 51.6 |
| random | chronological | 4,146 | 96.8% | 1,515/1,559 | 60.2 |
| best_fit | chronological | 4,169 | 97.4% | 1,518/1,559 | 14.8 |
| best_fit | constrained_first | 4,151 | 96.9% | 1,516/1,559 | 14.4 |

Best-fit ranking cuts wasted seats by 71% vs first-fit (60.2 for random) and changes the placement rate by +0.6 percentage points. Most-constrained-first ordering changed it by -0.4 points, so the simple chronological policy is the default.

## 3. Timetable repair (greedy, never creates a new clash)
- Double-booked slots: 1,990 -> 825
- Over-crowded classes: 2,009 -> 1,236
- Mean seat utilisation: 71.6% -> 75.4% (1,799 proposed moves)

## 4. Learned models vs baselines (chronological splits)
- Demand forecast (Poisson GLM): MAE 1.401 vs best baseline 1.399; beats baseline: **False**.
- Unmet-request classifier: ROC-AUC logistic 0.506, boosting 0.486 (0.5 = chance); signal found: **False**.

Interpretation: request attributes carry no usable signal for forecasting demand or outcomes in this synthetic dataset, so the product value comes from the exact constraint-based allocator rather than from a learned predictor. The learned models are kept as audited experiments and reported honestly.
